hero.lead: A nation of 45.9 million with farmland across four tenths of its land, where the IMF approved a $20 billion programme in April 2025 and the World Bank finances early childhood and foundational literacy.

capital.heading: Capital for stability, and for children who must learn to read.

register.name: Resilient Infrastructure for Regional Economic Development and Job Creation, Salta
register.note: Shown as Approved on the World Bank’s Finances One page, data as of 30 September 2026
register.text: A World Bank loan for resilient infrastructure and basic services that support jobs in the province of Salta. It serves the livelihood standard and the basic services behind the other standards in the province.

register.name: Guarantees for commercial financing (IBRD and MIGA)
register.detail: World Bank and MIGA · P516354 · approved 16 June 2026 · IBRD first-loss Policy-Based Guarantee and MIGA second-loss guarantee · six-year loan, three-year grace period
register.note: IBRD commitment of US$1.2 billion (P516354) on the World Bank’s Finances One page; the guarantees cover 95% of debt service
register.text: Two World Bank Group guarantees, approved by the World Bank and MIGA Boards on 16 June 2026, that help mobilise up to $2 billion in commercial loans for Argentina. They support a reform agenda aimed at creating jobs and attracting investment into infrastructure, and serve the livelihood standard and the public finances behind all seven.

register.name: Supporting the Transition to Sustainable Electricity and Gas Sectors
register.detail: World Bank · P506430 · approved 18 December 2025 · press release of 19 December 2025
register.note: Shown as Approved on the World Bank’s Finances One page, data as of 30 September 2026
register.text: A World Bank loan that expands support for a sustainable electricity and gas sector in Argentina. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Resilient Infrastructure for Regional Economic Development and Job Creation, Phase 1, Neuquén
register.note: Shown as Approved on the World Bank’s Finances One page, data as of 30 September 2026
register.text: The first phase of a World Bank programme for resilient infrastructure, regional economic development and job creation, for the province of Neuquén. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility
register.detail: IMF · approved 11 April 2025 · SDR 15.267 billion, 479% of quota · second review completed 21 May 2026
register.note: About US$15.8 billion (SDR 11.452 billion) disbursed by 21 May 2026
register.text: An IMF arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility that supports Argentina’s economic programme. Completion of the second review on 21 May 2026 made about US$1 billion (SDR 0.8 billion) available, bringing disbursements to about US$15.8 billion. It steadies the public finances that fund all seven standards.

register.name: Development Policy Financing
register.detail: World Bank · approved 11 April 2025 · budget support · part of a US$12 billion World Bank Group package
register.text: World Bank budget support approved on 11 April 2025, part of a US$12 billion World Bank Group package. It backs reforms that improve social transfer programmes for vulnerable households, make the tax system more progressive and streamline energy subsidies, and serves the livelihood and energy standards.

register.name: Integrated Early Childhood Development
register.note: Approved on the same day as the Foundational Literacy loan
register.text: A World Bank loan for care, health and early learning for young children. It serves the health and education standards from the first years of life.

register.name: Foundational Literacy
register.note: Aimed at the standard furthest from reach in Argentina, education
register.text: A World Bank loan for reading and writing in the early grades of primary school. It serves the education standard, where 59.1% of children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school on 2019 data.

register.name: Human Capital Strengthening Support Program
register.detail: IDB · approved by the Board of Executive Directors · social protection, education and employment
register.note: Listed as approved on the IDB’s Argentina country page, read 17 November 2026
register.text: An IDB operation to strengthen Argentina’s social protection system, helping students stay in school and expanding access to employment opportunities. It serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Energy Sector Sustainability Programme (SWAp)
register.detail: CAF · loan contract model approved by Decree 23/2026 of 18 January 2026 · executed by the Ministry of Economy through the Secretariat of Energy
register.note: Up to USD 400,000,000, as stated in the decree
register.text: A CAF loan for a sector-wide programme that strengthens the sustainability of the energy sector through better targeting of energy subsidies to vulnerable households and the promotion of energy efficiency. It serves the energy standard and protects poorer households as subsidies are reformed.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Southern beech forest beside a lake in the Andes of Argentina

items.name: Agua Segura
items.text: Brings innovative water-treatment technology and hygiene training to schools and community centres. With Opella, its “Manos al Agua” initiative is installing ultrafiltration in twenty-six institutions in the Buenos Aires metropolitan area and the interior, with a focus on Salta, to reach more than 5,500 people in 2025.

items.name: Fundación Multipolar
items.text: Helps people living on the street rebuild independent lives over 12 to 18 months, with work as the main tool: therapy, job training, a school of productive entrepreneurship and placement in cooperatives. The City of Buenos Aires enlisted it to manage the district’s largest shelters, which aid around 8,000 people a day, and it had placed 113 people in paid work since June 2019.

items.name: Mamotest
items.text: An impact company born in Corrientes that brings high-quality studies for the early detection of breast cancer to places traditional health systems do not reach. Its own artificial intelligence algorithm helps doctors read mammograms.

items.name: Arbusta
items.text: A technology services company that hires and trains young people aged 18 to 28 with no work experience, a model begun in 2013 for young people from vulnerable neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires. It now trains and validates artificial intelligence for companies, combining technology with human work.

items.name: Asteroid (Háblalo)
items.text: The creator of Háblalo, a free communication app used by more than 500,000 people with disabilities in 75 countries. Through Háblalo for Employment it now also helps them into customer service jobs; a finalist for the 2026 Premio a la Innovación con Impacto of Fundación Banco Nación and Endeavor Argentina.
